{{Use mdy dates|date=July 2025}}
'''A. Douglas Stone''' is the Carl Morse Professor of Applied Physics and Physics at [[Yale University]]. He was the 2014 recipient of the [[Phi Beta Kappa Award in Science|Phi Beta Kappa Award]] in Science for his book ''Einstein and the Quantum: The Quest of the Valiant Swabian''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://appliedphysics.yale.edu/douglas-stone|title=A. Douglas Stone {{!}} Department of Applied Physics|website=appliedphysics.yale.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-09-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencefriday.com/person/a-douglas-stone/|title=A. Douglas Stone|website=Science Friday|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://press.princeton.edu/titles/10068.html|title=Einstein and the Quantum|website=Princeton University Press|language=en|access-date=2019-09-29}}</ref>

He has a Ph.D. in Physics from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]], a social studies degree from [[Harvard University|Harvard]] and degrees in physics and philosophy from [[Oxford University]]. He was a [[Rhodes Scholarship|Rhodes Scholar]] in 1976, An [[Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellow]] in 1990, an [[American Physical Society]] Fellow in 1993 and a fellow of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]] in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eng.yale.edu/stonegroup/|title=A. Douglas Stone Research Group|website=www.eng.yale.edu|access-date=2019-09-29}}</ref>

== Awards ==
